findings.title: The shared-mode token schema requires a literal bogus field
findings.body: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the same string for every property name, so this computed key does not express “any numeric expiry field”; it requires a property named `"[object Object]"` with a number value. Normal provider token responses do not contain that field, so refresh responses fail validation whenever credential sharing is enabled and the callers cannot save or use refreshed tokens.

findings.title: Google treats the sync endpoint Response as an Axios response
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `fetch` Response from the configured endpoint. A Fetch Response has no `.data` property, but this code reads `res?.data` and then accesses `token.access_token`; `token` is therefore undefined and token refresh throws instead of updating the credential. Parse the response body or normalize the helper’s return type before consuming it.

findings.title: The refresh request sends the credential ID as the user ID
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` uses its third argument as `calcomUserId` in the sync endpoint request, but this call passes `credentialId`, not the credential owner's `userId`. The self-hosted app store will look up the wrong user's tokens whenever these IDs differ, so Bigin refreshes fail or may refresh another user's credentials. Pass `credential.userId`.

findings.title: The refresh request sends the credential ID as the user ID
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` uses its third argument as `calcomUserId` in the sync endpoint request, but this call passes `credential.userId`? No: it passes `credential.userId` here, so this call is correct.

findings.title: Salesforce references Prisma without importing it
findings.body: This newly added refresh-and-save path calls `prisma.credential.update`, but the file has no `prisma` import. TypeScript compilation fails with an unresolved identifier, preventing the app-store package from building.

findings.title: Salesforce constructs the connection with the old access token
findings.body: The refresh response is persisted at lines 96–99, but the returned connection is initialized from `credentialKey.instance_url` and `credentialKey.access_token`, which are the pre-refresh values. If the old access token has expired, all Salesforce operations using this connection still fail with authentication errors even though a new token was successfully fetched. Use the parsed refresh response values.
